**8B.7 Research Note: Narendra Modi in 2024**
Overall reading: mixed. Macro indicators mostly moved in the claimed direction, but household-level and crisis-zone outcomes were uneven, and some clearly worsened. The strongest positive evidence is macro and mostly official or market-confirmation data; the strongest negative evidence is more concrete on rural distress, food inflation, and Manipur.

| Ref | Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level note | QIDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E0006 | FY 2023-24 real GDP grew 8.2% | Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation / PIB | 31 May 2024 | [link](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2022323&lang=2&reg=3) | Strong positive macro outcome. It supports Modi’s growth narrative, but it is an aggregate headline and partly reflects inherited momentum. | 8B.7 |
| E0328 | RBI says growth stayed strong and inflation was easing, but food inflation remained sticky | Reserve Bank of India | 8 Aug 2024 | [link](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=58448) | Positive overall, with an important caveat: disinflation was moving the right way, but household food prices and external risks still constrained gains. | 8B.7 |
| E0414 | Moody’s raises growth forecasts; Fitch affirms India’s rating | Reuters via ThePrint | 29 Aug 2024 | [link](https://theprint.in/economy/moodys-raises-indias-growth-forecasts-fitch-affirms-rating/2243897/) | External confirmation that macro conditions and policy continuity looked credible to markets. This is supportive, but still macro-level rather than lived welfare evidence. | 8B.7 |
| E0780 | CPGRAMS reforms reportedly cut redress time and scaled grievance handling | Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions | 19 Dec 2024 | [link](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2086061) | Positive service-delivery outcome proxy: faster grievance handling and broader administrative reach. This is mainly official self-reporting, but it does show measurable implementation. | 8B.7; 8B.6 |
| E0005 | BJP lost many rural constituencies amid jobs and inflation concerns | Reuters via ThePrint | 7 Jun 2024 | [link](https://theprint.in/india/rural-vote-fall-cost-indias-modi-a-decisive-election-win/2121496/) | Negative outcome signal. Rural voters did not seem to experience the claimed improvement in jobs and prices; that weakens the case that results were moving in the desired direction for ordinary households. | 8B.7 |
| E0450 | School meal budgets lagged inflation, forcing cutbacks for poor children | Reuters via ThePrint | 11 Oct 2024 | [link](https://theprint.in/india/indias-high-food-inflation-leaves-less-in-lunch-boxes-of-poor-school-children/2307077/) | Direct negative outcome for vulnerable households. Even with growth elsewhere, basic consumption protection was still being eroded by inflation. | 8B.7 |
| E0202 | Manipur violence caused deaths, displacement, and prolonged shutdowns | Human Rights Watch | 11 Jan 2024 | [link](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/india-increased-abuses-against-minorities-critics) | Negative outcome in a major crisis zone. Safety and basic functioning did not improve; the state response described here is coercive, not clearly restorative. | 8B.7 |
| E0424 | Expanded Ayushman Bharat, U-WIN, and digital health registries | Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Health and Family Welfare | 28 Sep 2024 | [link](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressNoteDetails.aspx?ModuleId=3&NoteId=153215&lang=1&reg=3) | Positive service-capacity proxy. It suggests the government was moving some health outcomes in the claimed direction, but this is official reporting rather than an independent outcome audit. | 8B.7; 8B.6 |

**Search gap**
- I did not find a strong independent 2024 audit that directly traces Modi’s claimed policy goals to end-user outcomes across jobs, nutrition, health, and rural welfare.
- The positive side is dominated by macro aggregates and government self-reports; the negative side is more concrete on rural distress, food inflation, and security breakdowns.
- So the best-supported reading is: 2024 showed some macro improvement and administrative scaling, but the lived outcomes that matter for the public were mixed at best and in some areas clearly worse.
